key_insight: AI is shifting research from a craft-based human process to an automated pipeline, creating both major opportunity and serious structural risks.
engineering_relevance: For computational science and engineering, this means AI systems can accelerate discovery workflows, but they also require strong governance, validation, and human oversight to avoid compounding errors and misuse.
method: Frames research as an end-to-end pipeline rather than isolated expert tasks.
Analyzes seven consequences of AI-driven science, from competence loss to agenda capture.
Uses the US DOE Genesis Mission as a concrete example of this broader shift.
evidence_signal: The abstract is a conceptual essay rather than an empirical study, so its claims are based on structured argumentation and program analysis, not reported experimental data.
watch_item: Closed-loop AI research pipelines may amplify systematic errors unless human review, transparency, and robust evaluation are preserved.
paper_title: The Industrialization of Research ; On AI-Driven Science and Its Consequences
